preset_notes.custom: Fill in your provider's URL, headers (e.g. an API key), and body shape yourself. {{phone}} and {{message}} are substituted in wherever they appear, in the URL, headers, or body.
preset_notes.teltonika_rutos_legacy: Teltonika removed this method in RutOS 7.14+. Only use this preset if your router is confirmed still running an older firmware version -- otherwise use the token-based preset above.
preset_notes.teltonika_rutos_new: RUTOS 7.14+ requires a bearer token obtained by logging into your router's API first (see your router's API documentation, usually at https://<router-ip>/api-docs) -- paste the token into the Authorization header above. Tokens can expire; if sending suddenly stops working, this is usually why.
preset_notes.twilio_sms: Replace {account_sid} in the URL and {your_twilio_number} in the body with your own values. Set Basic Auth below using your Account SID as the username and your Auth Token as the password.
preset_notes.twilio_voice: Same Account SID / Auth Token as Twilio SMS above. The Twiml parameter's <Say> verb is what makes Twilio read the alert text aloud on the call.

bandwidth_pct.hint: Interface utilisation. Sustained high values mean the link is close to saturation.
bandwidth_pct.label: Bandwidth usage

connect_ms.good: under 100 ms in the same region, under 300 ms overseas
connect_ms.hint: Time to open the network connection to the server. Pure network distance/congestion; high with a fast server = a network path problem.
connect_ms.label: TCP connect time

cpu_pct.hint: Processor load. Sustained high load = a runaway process or an under-sized machine.
cpu_pct.label: CPU usage

disk_pct.hint: Space used on the monitored disk or share. A full disk stops databases, logs and updates.
disk_pct.label: Disk usage

dns_ms.hint: Time to turn the site name into an IP address. High = slow or failing DNS server.
dns_ms.label: DNS lookup time

latency_ms.good: under 50 ms on a LAN, under 150 ms across a WAN
latency_ms.hint: Ping round-trip time to the device. High = congested link, overloaded device or a long path.
latency_ms.label: Latency

memory_pct.hint: RAM in use. Near 100 % the system starts swapping and slows down or kills processes.
memory_pct.label: Memory usage

packet_loss_pct.hint: Share of ping packets that got no reply. Anything above 0 on a wired link deserves a look.
packet_loss_pct.label: Packet loss

response_ms.hint: Time until the site starts answering (DNS + connect + TLS + server think time, redirects included). High = slow or overloaded server, heavy page, or a poor network path.
response_ms.label: Response time

ssl_days_left.hint: Days until the site's certificate expires. ALERTS WHEN THE VALUE FALLS BELOW the threshold. At 0 the certificate is expired and browsers block the site.
ssl_days_left.label: SSL certificate expires in

ssl_handshake_ms.hint: Time to negotiate the encrypted connection after it opens. High = distant or overloaded server/proxy, or very heavy TLS settings.
ssl_handshake_ms.label: SSL handshake time

placeholders.description: The device/site's host, IP address, or URL.
Raw metric key that triggered this alert.
Human-readable metric name with its unit, e.g. Response time (ms), SSL certificate expires in (days).
The value that triggered this alert.
The threshold that was crossed, with its unit (e.g. 1000 ms, or below 30 days for SSL expiry). Shows an em-dash if not applicable to this alert.
Raw state: warning, critical, offline, or recovered.
Display label shown in the subject/banner (automatically becomes e.g. 'ESCALATION L2' once an escalation level fires).
Hex color associated with this state/level -- for use in custom HTML styling.
Per-state dark background color for the email card (a subtly different tint for warning/critical/offline/recovered).
THE DASHBOARD LINK. Automatically matches however your team actually accesses the server (PC name or IP) -- see app.py's _remember_access_host().
Current Net-monit version, normally shown in the footer.
0 for a normal (non-escalated) alert; 1, 2, or 3 once that escalation level has fired.
Pre-built HTML escalation banner snippet, ready to drop straight into an HTML template. Empty string when escalation_level is 0. Not meaningful in a plain-text template.
